papers.title: MultiTargetDB: a comprehensive database of multitarget ligands for polypharmacology research and drug discovery.
papers.abstract: Multitarget drug discovery has gained considerable traction in recent years, particularly for the treatment of complex diseases. Despite the growing demand for dedicated, well-curated resources to advance polypharmacology research and rational multitarget drug discovery, such resources remain severely limited. Here, we present MultiTargetDB, a database of multitarget ligands integrated with comprehensive biological annotations and measurement-level provenance. At the small molecule level, MultiTargetDB integrates chemical structures (including molecular scaffolds), their drug development stage
papers.summary: MultiTargetDB is a new database that collects multitarget ligands—small molecules that bind multiple biological targets—along with detailed biological annotations and measurement-level provenance. It integrates chemical structures, molecular scaffolds, and drug development stages to support polypharmacology research and rational multitarget drug discovery. The resource addresses the shortage of well-curated, dedicated databases for multitarget drug development.

papers.title: Computational network pharmacology and molecular simulations to explore the potential mechanisms of Pyrrosia piloselloides compounds against prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer is major cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality in men worldwide. Emerging evidence highlights the dragon scale fern (Pyrrosia piloselloides or P. piloselloides) has demonstrated anticancer potential, but its molecular mechanisms against prostate cancer remain unclear. The study aimed to investigate its potential anticancer compounds and underlying molecular mechanisms using an integrated in silico approach.
papers.journal: Journal of the Egyptian National Cancer Institute
papers.summary: This study uses computational network pharmacology and molecular dynamics simulations to predict which compounds from the dragon scale fern (Pyrrosia piloselloides) might act against prostate cancer and through which molecular targets. The authors identify candidate phytochemicals and their likely protein targets, then use docking and simulation to assess binding stability. The work is entirely in silico and provides hypotheses rather than experimental validation.

papers.title: From LC-MS Metabolomic Profiling to AIEnabled Navigation of NPs Chemical Space: Recent Advances and Emerging Directions.
papers.abstract: Natural products (NPs) occupy a unique region of chemical space and continue to provide privileged scaffolds for drug discovery, chemical ecology, and biotechnology. However, the exploration of NP diversity remains constrained by the complexity of biological extracts, the low annotation rate of LC-MS features, and the rediscovery of known metabolites. Recent advances in LC-HRMS/MS-based metabolomics, coupled with expanding spectral and structural databases, molecular networking, and in silico annotation methods, have considerably improved the characterization of complex metabolomes and facilit
papers.summary: This review discusses how LC-MS metabolomic profiling, combined with expanding spectral databases, molecular networking, and in silico annotation, is improving the characterization of complex natural product extracts. It highlights how AI-enabled navigation of natural product chemical space can help overcome low annotation rates and rediscovery of known metabolites, accelerating natural product-based drug discovery.

papers.title: Modeling ethnic differences via drug-predicted clearance from chemical structures.
papers.abstract: Ethnic differences in pharmacokinetics can result in clinically relevant differences in drug efficacy and safety, even when identical doses are administered. Although mechanistic approaches such as physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling can be used to evaluate population-specific pharmacokinetics, there remains a need for complementary screening approaches that can assess ethnic difference risk at very early stages of drug discovery with limited experimental information. The aim of this study was to develop a machine-learning-based approach to assess the risk of ethnic differences in o
papers.journal: European journal of pharmaceutical sciences : official journal of the European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences
papers.summary: The authors developed a machine-learning approach that predicts drug clearance from chemical structure alone and uses it to flag the risk of ethnic differences in pharmacokinetics early in drug discovery. This complements resource-intensive physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling by enabling screening with limited experimental data.

papers.title: DockBind: A Quality-Controlled Data Set of Modeled Protein-Ligand Complexes Associated with Affinity Data.
papers.abstract: Ligand-protein interaction prediction is essential for structure-based drug discovery, but further development of machine-learning scoring functions is limited by a lack of high-quality training data sets. Here, we present DockBind, a curated data set of modeled protein-ligand complexes paired with experimental binding affinity data, generated through a quality-controlled docking workflow. This workflow was developed based on an expanded docking benchmark, where we systematically evaluated free and template-based docking methods as well as ligand similarity and maximum common substructure (MCS
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: DockBind is a curated dataset of modeled protein-ligand complexes paired with experimental binding affinity data, created through a quality-controlled docking workflow. The authors benchmarked free and template-based docking methods along with ligand similarity and maximum common substructure approaches to build this resource, aiming to address the shortage of high-quality training data for machine-learning scoring functions in structure-based drug discovery.

papers.title: Structure-function relationships in a square-planar Cu(ii) hybrid halometalate: experimental, DFT, molecular docking, optical, and biological studies.
papers.abstract: A novel organic-inorganic copper(ii) hybrid halometalate, (C6H8BrN2)2[CuBr4], was successfully synthesized and investigated using complementary experimental and computational approaches. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis revealed discrete square-planar [CuBr4]2- anions embedded within a three-dimensional supramolecular architecture stabilized by N-H⋯Br hydrogen bonds, π-π stacking interactions, and halogen contacts. Optical studies indicated semiconducting characteristics with an estimated band gap of approximately 2.5 eV, together with a broad visible emission assigned to ligand-to-me
papers.summary: The authors synthesized a new organic-inorganic copper(II) hybrid halometalate, (C6H8BrN2)2[CuBr4], and characterized it using X-ray crystallography, optical spectroscopy, DFT calculations, molecular docking, and biological assays. The material features discrete square-planar [CuBr4]2- anions held in a 3D supramolecular network by hydrogen bonds, π-π stacking, and halogen contacts, and shows semiconducting behavior with a ~2.5 eV band gap plus broad visible emission. The work links the crystal structure to optical and biological properties through combined experimental and computational analysis.

papers.title: In Silico Investigation of Candidate Anticancer Targets for Aryltetralin Lignans Previously Reported from Cleistanthus Species.
papers.abstract: Aryltetralin lignans isolated from the fruits of Cleistanthus species exhibit substantial cytotoxic activity, although the molecular interactions underlying these effects remain incompletely understood. This study combined computational target investigation with previously published experimental chemical characterization and cytotoxic evidence and no new isolation or cytotoxicity experiments were carried out. Cleistantoxin, 7-hydroxypicropolygamain, neo-cleistantoxin, cleisindoside A, cleisindoside D, and cleistonkinin D were previously isolated from C. indochinensis, C. tonkinensis, C. eberha
papers.summary: This study uses computational docking and target-prediction approaches to investigate which protein targets might mediate the anticancer activity of six aryltetralin lignans previously isolated from Cleistanthus species. No new compounds were isolated and no new experiments were performed; the work integrates prior chemical and cytotoxicity data with in silico target fishing. The authors propose candidate anticancer targets for these lignans, offering hypotheses to guide future experimental validation.

papers.title: A Pathway-Driven Computational Drug Discovery Framework Integrating Machine Learning and Virtual Screening for Identification of Anti-Rheumatoid Arthritis Natural Small Molecules.
papers.abstract: Objective: This study aimed to establish a pathway-driven computational drug discovery framework integrating machine learning, target prioritization, virtual screening, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and in vitro evaluation to identify natural small molecules with potential anti-rheumatoid arthritis (RA) activity. Methods: Sixteen RA-related Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets were included, with 15 cohorts used for model development and one reserved for independent external validation. Pathway features quantified by gene set variation analysis (GSVA) were subjected to cohort-aware fe
papers.summary: This study presents an integrated computational pipeline combining machine learning on pathway-level features from 16 RA GEO datasets, target prioritization, virtual screening, and MD simulations to identify natural small molecules with potential anti-rheumatoid arthritis activity, followed by in vitro validation. The framework demonstrates how pathway-driven feature engineering can guide drug repurposing or natural product discovery for complex diseases.

papers.title: Computational Identification of GABA-A Receptor Ligands Targeting the Histamine Allosteric Pocket.
papers.abstract: The γ-aminobutyric acid type A (GABA-A) receptor is a key regulator of inhibitory neurotransmission in the central nervous system, and a promising target for cognitive and neurological disorders. Histamine interacts with a distinct allosteric pocket located at the β3-β3 subunit interface, providing an opportunity for the discovery of novel ligands. In the present study, an integrated in silico workflow combining ligand-based similarity analysis, ADMET filtering, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations was applied to identify candidate ligands for this histamine-associated site. D
papers.summary: This study used a computational pipeline—ligand similarity screening, ADMET filtering, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations—to identify candidate compounds that bind the histamine allosteric pocket at the β3-β3 interface of the GABA-A receptor. The work nominates putative ligands for a less-explored allosteric site relevant to cognitive and neurological disorders, but the findings are purely in silico and require experimental validation.

papers.title: Navigating the Eukaryotic Paradox: Insights for AI-Driven Computational Strategies Against Antifungal Resistance.
papers.abstract: The escalating crisis of invasive fungal infections and increasing antifungal resistance demand rapid therapeutic innovation. Given the critically narrow clinical arsenal, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have emerged as pivotal strategies to accelerate drug repurposing, providing a rapid alternative to de novo drug discovery. However, translational success in medical mycology faces a major biological hurdle: the "eukaryotic paradox," the extensive genomic, metabolic, and structural homology between fungal cells and human hosts. This review provides a critical and compara
papers.summary: This review examines how AI and machine learning can accelerate antifungal drug repurposing, but highlights a major obstacle: the 'eukaryotic paradox,' where fungi share extensive genomic, metabolic, and structural similarities with human hosts. The authors critically compare computational strategies and discuss how this homology complicates the discovery of selective fungal targets.

papers.title: From Mechanistic Models to AI Synergy: A Roadmap for Predictive and Personalized Biology.
papers.abstract: Two paradigms now drive the life sciences. One is the explanatory depth of mathematical modeling, the other the predictive power of artificial intelligence. For decades, mechanistic models have offered a rigorous, hypothesis-driven framework for dissecting biological processes, while AI has proven itself at finding patterns in the large, high-dimensional datasets of modern biology. Each has delivered major advances on its own. Together they promise a synthesis that could redefine the boundaries of biological inquiry. In this review we propose a three-part taxonomy of integration strategies, na
papers.summary: This review proposes a three-part taxonomy for integrating mechanistic mathematical models with artificial intelligence in the life sciences. The authors argue that combining hypothesis-driven mechanistic modeling with AI's pattern-finding power on large, high-dimensional datasets can yield a synthesis more powerful than either approach alone. The paper serves as a roadmap toward predictive and personalized biology.

papers.title: QSAR-Guided In Silico Design of Piperazinylanthranilamide Factor Xa Inhibitors: Applicability-Domain Assessment, ADMET Profiling, Molecular Docking, Molecular Dynamics, and MM/GBSA.
papers.abstract: An integrated computational workflow was developed to prioritize piperazinylanthranilamide factor Xa (FXa) inhibitor candidates. Twenty literature compounds were geometry-optimized and described using alvaDesc to construct a constrained additive multivariate adaptive regression splines model. Internal validation and an assessment of the applicability domain guided the evaluation of 20 prospective analogs. Ten selected analogs and two same-series references were docked to FXa, with apixaban as the crystallographic comparator. Thirteen initial 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations were supplemen
papers.summary: This study uses an integrated computational pipeline—QSAR modeling, applicability-domain assessment, ADMET profiling, molecular docking, 100 ns molecular dynamics, and MM/GBSA—to prioritize piperazinylanthranilamide analogs as factor Xa inhibitors. Twenty literature compounds were used to build a constrained MARS model, which guided the evaluation of 20 prospective analogs; ten selected analogs were then docked and simulated against FXa with apixaban as comparator. The work demonstrates a workflow for virtual screening and prioritization of anticoagulant candidates prior to synthesis.

papers.title: Donor-Resolved Analysis of HES1-Associated Fibroblast States in Systemic Sclerosis.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: We examined HES1-associated fibroblast states in systemic sclerosis (SSc) and the rationale for testing upstream γ-secretase inhibition with nirogacestat. Methods: We analysed 325,636 skin cells from 230 donors across five non-redundant cohorts using complete computational transcription-factor screens, donor-level activity and trajectory analyses, multiome data and spatial assays. Donors or independent simulations were the inference units, with cohort adjustment and multiplicity correction where applicable. Three independent 200 ns molecular dynamics runs per condition c
papers.summary: This study analyzed over 325,000 skin cells from 230 donors across five cohorts to identify HES1-associated fibroblast states in systemic sclerosis (SSc), using transcription-factor screens, donor-level activity and trajectory analyses, multiome data, and spatial assays. The authors present a donor-resolved framework supporting the rationale for testing upstream γ-secretase inhibition with nirogacestat in SSc. The work emphasizes donor-level inference and cohort adjustment to identify fibroblast states linked to HES1 activity.

papers.title: The Application of Artificial Intelligence in Brucellosis: Diagnosis, Genomic Analysis, Epidemiological Prediction and Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Brucellosis, a globally significant zoonosis caused by Brucella, poses a substantial impediment to the sustainable development of the livestock industry and threatens public health security. Traditional control and prevention strategies for brucellosis suffer from fundamental limitations. These include the time-consuming, biosafety risks associated with bacterial culture and the difficulty in differentiating between natural infection and vaccine-induced immunity with serological tests. There remains a challenge in accurately distinguishing vaccine strains from wild-type strains via genotyping
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This review surveys how artificial intelligence is being applied across four areas of brucellosis research: clinical diagnosis, genomic analysis, epidemiological forecasting, and drug discovery. It highlights that traditional approaches—bacterial culture, serology, and genotyping—are slow, biosafety-risky, and struggle to distinguish vaccine from wild-type strains, and argues that AI methods offer promising alternatives. As a review, it synthesizes existing work rather than presenting new experimental results.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Guided Virtual Screening Identifies a Novel MELK-Targeted Antiproliferative Lead Compound with G2/M Arrest Activity in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer and Lung Adenocarcinoma Cells.
papers.abstract: Background: Maternal embryonic leucine zipper kinase (MELK) is a cell cycle-regulated serine/threonine kinase frequently overexpressed in human malignancies, and represents a promising anticancer drug target. Discovery of structurally novel, highly selective MELK inhibitors remains an unmet need. Methods: In the study, we implemented an integrated computational pipeline combining four machine learning regressors (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, LightGBM), hierarchical Glide docking (HTVS to SP to XP), MM/GBSA rescoring, ADMET prediction, and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations to
papers.summary: This study used an integrated computational pipeline—combining four machine learning regressors, hierarchical molecular docking, MM/GBSA rescoring, ADMET prediction, and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations—to virtually screen for novel MELK kinase inhibitors. The screen identified a lead compound that showed antiproliferative activity and G2/M cell cycle arrest in triple-negative breast cancer and lung adenocarcinoma cell lines. The work demonstrates a machine learning-guided virtual screening strategy for discovering structurally novel kinase inhibitors.

papers.title: Network Pharmacology of Natural Products from Computational Prediction to Experimental Validation.
papers.abstract: Natural products are important sources of bioactive compounds, but their complex chemical composition and multi-target effects make their mechanisms difficult to investigate using conventional approaches. Network pharmacology provides a systems-level framework for integrating chemical, biological, and disease-related information to investigate these complex interactions. This review describes the network pharmacology workflow, from active-compound screening, ADMET evaluation and target prediction to network construction and pathway enrichment, and the complementary roles of molecular docking a
papers.summary: This review outlines the network pharmacology workflow for studying natural products, covering active-compound screening, ADMET evaluation, target prediction, network construction, and pathway enrichment, along with the complementary roles of molecular docking and experimental validation. It provides a systems-level framework for investigating the multi-target mechanisms of complex natural product mixtures.

papers.title: A Computational Workflow Integrating Explainable AI and Database Mining for the Prioritization of Antimicrobial Natural Products.
papers.abstract: The escalating threat of antimicrobial resistance demands the discovery of antibacterial agents with unprecedented chemical scaffolds. Natural products have historically been the most prolific source of antibiotics, yet the vast majority of catalogued natural products remain untested for antimicrobial activity. Here we present Natural-Product Graph-language, Uncertainty-Aware Relational Discovery (NP-GUARD), a modular computational framework that reframes antimicrobial natural-product discovery as an uncertainty-aware, relational, multi-objective learning problem. NP-GUARD integrates six core
papers.summary: The authors present NP-GUARD, a modular computational framework that combines explainable AI with database mining to prioritize natural products for antimicrobial activity testing. It frames antimicrobial natural-product discovery as an uncertainty-aware, relational, multi-objective learning problem, integrating six core components to rank untested compounds. This offers a systematic way to triage the vast catalog of natural products and focus experimental screening on the most promising candidates.

papers.title: Advancing the Translational Pipeline: From In Vivo and In Vitro 2D Models to Next-Generation Cell Culture Models for Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Modelling and Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Background: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is still a global health challenge, as there is no effective treatment due to the inadequacy of conventional experimental platforms for comprehending pathogenic mechanisms and developing therapy. Objectives: This review details the recent progress and clinical utility of next-generation iPSC-derived 3D in vitro systems integrated with microfluidics, CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, multi-omics readouts, and AI-based machine learning, which are emerging as transformative platforms for recapitulating key ALS pathological hallmarks. Methods: A literature s
papers.summary: This review surveys next-generation ALS disease models, arguing that conventional 2D cultures and animal models are insufficient for understanding pathogenesis and developing therapies. It highlights iPSC-derived 3D systems combined with microfluidics, CRISPR-Cas9 editing, multi-omics, and AI/ML as transformative platforms that better recapitulate ALS hallmarks and could improve drug discovery translation.

papers.title: DeepAVPred: A Deep Learning Framework Integrating RECM-DWT and BiGRU for Accurate Antiviral Peptide Prediction.
papers.abstract: Viral infections continue to pose a significant global health challenge. Antiviral peptides (AVPs) have emerged as promising therapeutic agents owing to their high specificity, favorable safety profiles, and broad-spectrum antiviral activity. However, experimental AVP identification is time-consuming and costly, while existing computational predictors often have limitations in predictive accuracy and feature representation. Here, we propose DeepAVPred, a deep learning-based framework for AVP identification. DeepAVPred integrates complementary sequence descriptors to capture physicochemical pro
papers.summary: DeepAVPred is a deep learning framework for predicting antiviral peptides from sequence, combining a new residue-level encoding method (RECM-DWT) with a bidirectional GRU network. It aims to improve on existing computational predictors that struggle with accuracy and feature representation, offering a faster alternative to costly experimental identification of antiviral peptides.

papers.title: In Silico Discovery of a Potential PI3Kα Inhibitor Incorporating an Imidazole Moiety for Breast Cancer Treatment.
papers.abstract: Excessive activation of PI3Kα is prevalent in breast cancer, aberrantly activating the PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway to drive tumor progression, thus rendering PI3Kα a vital therapeutic target. Two PI3Kα inhibitors (alpelisib and inavolisib) have been approved for clinical application. Inavolisib exerts a mutation-selective degradation mechanism and functions by directly eliminating aberrant proteins. To develop novel PI3Kα inhibitors, we employed multiple computational strategies including scaffold hopping based on the structure of inavolisib, -CDOCKER docking, Lipinski's rule of five, ADMET predicti
papers.summary: The authors used computational methods—scaffold hopping from the approved PI3Kα inhibitor inavolisib, molecular docking, Lipinski/ADMET filtering—to identify a novel imidazole-containing compound predicted to inhibit PI3Kα for breast cancer. The work is purely in silico, with no experimental validation reported in the abstract, so the candidate remains hypothetical.

papers.title: Deep Learning-Driven Identification and Experimental Validation of COX-2 and ERK1/2 as Anti-Inflammatory Targets of Avenanthramides.
papers.abstract: Chronic low-grade inflammation underlies numerous chronic diseases, yet the molecular targets of dietary bioactive compounds remain largely unknown.
papers.summary: This study uses deep learning to predict molecular targets of avenanthramides, oat-derived polyphenols, and experimentally validates COX-2 and ERK1/2 as anti-inflammatory targets. The work links dietary compounds to specific inflammatory pathways, supporting their potential in managing chronic low-grade inflammation.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics-Guided Triage of Approved Drugs Against Escherichia coli Resistance Targets Nominates Capmatinib, Metergoline and Nilotinib as Candidates for Experimental Testing.
papers.abstract: Virtual screening ranks compounds by scoring functions that correlate with molecular size, and hit lists are rarely benchmarked against compounds of established activity. We screened 2070 approved drugs against four Escherichia coli targets selected by pocket-druggability triage (FabI, LpxC, DHFR and GyrB), with each docking protocol validated by redocking its native ligand (RMSD 0.50-0.69 Å). Per target, the two top-scoring compounds and a reference inhibitor were simulated for 100 ns in triplicate (12 complexes, 3.6 μs). Docking did not recover the references: trimethoprim ranked 762/2068 an
papers.summary: The authors docked 2070 approved drugs against four E. coli antibacterial targets and then ran 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations on top hits plus reference inhibitors. Docking failed to recover known reference inhibitors (e.g., trimethoprim ranked 762nd), highlighting scoring-function bias, but MD triage nominated capmatinib, metergoline, and nilotinib as candidates for experimental testing. The work is a computational repurposing screen with no experimental validation yet.

papers.title: Language of Toxicity: An eXplainable Artificial Intelligence Approach.
papers.abstract: Toxicity prediction in small molecules represents a fundamental challenge in drug development and chemical safety assessment. Traditional approaches heavily rely on predefined molecular descriptors or fingerprints, potentially limiting the ability to capture complex and nonlinear structure-activity relationships. Here, we present a descriptor-free, language-inspired framework that can be applied to different toxicity prediction tasks within a unified architecture. The model proposed combines a multiscale Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) layer to capture chemical patterns at different scales
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: The authors introduce a descriptor-free, language-inspired deep learning framework for predicting small-molecule toxicity. It uses a multiscale CNN to capture chemical patterns at different scales within a unified architecture applicable to multiple toxicity prediction tasks, aiming to overcome limitations of predefined molecular descriptors and fingerprints.

papers.title: Senescence-Associated Transcriptome Reversal Prioritizes Repurposing Candidates for Diabetic Kidney Disease: A Computational Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a leading cause of end-stage kidney disease, and cellular senescence is a tractable therapeutic target; yet prioritizing credible repurposing candidates is difficult because bulk-tissue senescence signals are weak, single-dataset analyses are unstable, and transcriptome-reversal screens overstate novelty. The objective was to build a senescence-anchored, multi-evidence computational prioritization of repurposing candidates for DKD entirely from open data. Methods: Per-sample senescence activity was quantified by single-sample gene set enr
papers.summary: This computational study integrates multiple open transcriptomic datasets to quantify per-sample senescence activity in diabetic kidney disease and uses transcriptome-reversal screening to prioritize drug repurposing candidates. The authors address known pitfalls of bulk-tissue senescence signals and single-dataset instability by combining multiple lines of evidence. The work is a hypothesis-generating prioritization exercise rather than experimental validation.

papers.title: Validated Semantic Scoring Improves Filtering of Generic Concepts from Knowledge Graphs for Drug Repurposing Queries.
papers.abstract: When an ontology-based biomedical knowledge graph (a KG, containing information about genes, pathways, phenotypes, and molecular interactions) is analyzed using a computational reasoning system, the system can return unwanted generic concepts. Such generic concepts, in the context of a query about potential drug treatments for a disease, might include 'pharmaceutical preparations' or 'antibiotics'. Answers can be filtered based on hand-curated block-lists or ontology Information Content (IC), but to our knowledge, (1) neither filtering method has been validated against expert judgments of gene
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This paper introduces a validated semantic scoring method to filter out generic concepts (like 'pharmaceutical preparations') from ontology-based biomedical knowledge graphs when querying for drug repurposing candidates. The authors show that their approach outperforms existing filtering methods (hand-curated block-lists and information content) when validated against expert judgments. This improves the precision of computational reasoning systems for drug repurposing queries.

papers.title: An educational activity tailored for undergraduate students on AI-driven nanobody design for targeted antiviral therapeutics.
papers.abstract: Protein-based biologics are converging at an unprecedented pace as generative artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes early-stage drug discovery. Nanobodies, single-domain antibody fragments derived from camelid heavy chain-only immunoglobulins, are an emerging class of antiviral biologics prized for their small size, stability, and access to cryptic viral epitopes. Traditional nanobody discovery relies on animal immunization and phage display screening, a process that can take 6 to 12 months and is entirely inaccessible within a standard undergraduate laboratory session. Here, we describe a suc
papers.summary: This paper describes a short educational activity that teaches undergraduate students how to use generative AI tools to design nanobodies targeting viral proteins, replacing the months-long traditional immunization and phage display workflow. The activity aims to make cutting-edge AI-driven biologics design accessible within a standard lab session, giving students hands-on exposure to computational drug discovery concepts.

papers.title: Discovery of potential ALK inhibitors from Glycosmis phytochemicals via integrated machine learning and umbrella sampling approaches.
papers.abstract: Anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) is a key therapeutic target for various cancers because of its central role in tumor growth and survival signaling. This study employed an integrated computational workflow combining machine learning (ML), molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, umbrella sampling (US), and toxicity prediction to identify potential ALK inhibitors from 307 phytochemicals of the Glycosmis genus. A previously validated CatBoost regression model predicted binding free energies, leading to the selection of 26 compounds with ΔG ML < -11 kcal mol-1. Molecular docking id
papers.summary: This study used an integrated computational pipeline—combining machine learning (CatBoost regression), molecular docking, molecular dynamics, umbrella sampling, and toxicity prediction—to screen 307 phytochemicals from the Glycosmis genus for potential inhibitors of anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK), a cancer drug target. The ML model predicted binding free energies and narrowed the set to 26 compounds with ΔG < -11 kcal/mol, which were then evaluated by docking and free-energy methods. The work nominates candidate natural-product ALK inhibitors for further experimental validation.

papers.title: Design, synthesis, and docking analysis of benzene sulfonamide-[1,4]benzoxazepine hybrids as acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase inhibitors.
papers.abstract: A series of novel hybrid [1,4]benzoxazepine-based sulfonamide derivatives 9-12a-j were synthesized and evaluated for their inhibitory activity against acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and butyrylcholinesterase (BChE). Compounds 9a and 9b exhibited potent dual cholinesterase inhibition, with IC50 values of 9.04 and 8.61 µM against AChE and 3.08 and 4.64 µM against BChE, respectively. Compound 12j emerged as the most potent BChE inhibitor of the series (IC50 = 1.06 ± 0.11 µM), displaying pronounced BChE preference (SI = 10.37), whereas 9d showed the highest BChE selectivity (BChE IC50 = 4.18 ± 0.56 µ
papers.summary: The authors synthesized a series of hybrid molecules combining benzene sulfonamide and [1,4]benzoxazepine scaffolds and tested them as inhibitors of acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and butyrylcholinesterase (BChE), enzymes targeted in Alzheimer's disease. Several compounds showed micromolar dual inhibition, with compound 12j being the most potent BChE inhibitor (IC50 ~1 µM) and showing selectivity for BChE over AChE. Docking analysis was used to rationalize binding interactions.

papers.title: Innovative design and development of novel thiazole-paracetamol hybrids as COX inhibitors and immunomodulatory activity: design, synthesis, SAR, in vitro biological evaluation, and molecular docking analysis.
papers.abstract: The hybridization approach was employed to design a single pharmacophore based on the conjugation of paracetamol with thiazole derivatives, yielding thiazole-paracetamol hybrid derivatives 4-11 that utilize a linker from hydrazone (-C[double bond, length as m-dash]N-NH) and azo (-N[double bond, length as m-dash]N-) linkers, serving as the hydrogen bond donor/acceptor binding site. The structure of the designed derivatives was fully characterized and confirmed using analytical data (IR, 1H NMR, and 13C NMR), and elemental analysis. The anti-inflammatory potential of the synthesized hybrids was
papers.summary: This study designed and synthesized a series of thiazole-paracetamol hybrid molecules (compounds 4-11) linked via hydrazone or azo groups, aiming to combine COX inhibition with immunomodulatory activity in a single pharmacophore. The hybrids were fully characterized and evaluated in vitro for anti-inflammatory potential, with structure-activity relationships and molecular docking analyses used to rationalize binding to COX targets. The work represents a medicinal chemistry effort to repurpose paracetamol into more potent dual-action anti-inflammatory agents.

papers.title: Design, click synthesis, and biological evaluation of novel uracil-1,2,3-triazole hybrids as dual EGFR/CDK1 inhibitors: antiproliferative activity, mechanistic insights, and in silico studies.
papers.abstract: A novel series of uracil-1,2,3-triazole hybrids was designed, synthesized, and evaluated as dual EGFR/CDK1 inhibitors to target cancer cell proliferation and survival. Synthesis was initiated via the nucleophilic substitution of 2-chloro-N-(1,3-dimethyl-2,6-dioxo-pyrimidin-4-yl)acetamide (3) with sodium azide, yielding the key intermediate 4. Subsequent copper-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloadditions (CuAAC) with various terminal alkynes and 1,3-dicarbonyls afforded the target triazole analogues 6a,b, 8a-c, and 10b,c. In vitro antiproliferative screening against a panel of four human cancer cell
papers.summary: This study reports the design and click-chemistry synthesis of uracil-1,2,3-triazole hybrid compounds intended to act as dual inhibitors of EGFR and CDK1, two kinases important in cancer proliferation. The compounds were screened for antiproliferative activity against four human cancer cell lines, with mechanistic and in silico docking studies supporting the dual-target rationale. The work is a medicinal chemistry structure-activity exploration rather than a validated new therapeutic.

papers.title: Conversational Multi-Agentic Network-Driven Disease Module Identification and Drug Repurposing Prediction With ChatDRex: Platform Development Study.
papers.abstract: Repurposing approved drugs offers a time- and cost-effective alternative to traditional drug development. However, in silico prediction of repurposing candidates is challenging and requires the effective collaboration of specialists in various fields, including pharmacology, medicine, biology, and bioinformatics. Fragmented, specialized algorithms and tools often address only narrow aspects of the overall problem. Heterogeneous, unstructured data landscapes require the expertise of specialized users. Hence, diverse data sources might not integrate smoothly across workflows.
papers.summary: ChatDRex is a conversational multi-agent platform that integrates disease module identification and drug repurposing prediction into a single workflow. It uses multiple specialized agents coordinated through a chat interface to handle heterogeneous data sources and fragmented algorithms, aiming to make in silico repurposing more accessible to interdisciplinary users. The platform addresses the challenge of integrating diverse data and tools that typically require separate specialist expertise.

papers.title: ADMET property prediction and toxicity profiling of CDK2 inhibitors: a practical cheminformatics tutorial using ADMET-AI 2.0 and RDKit.
papers.abstract: Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, and Toxicity (ADMET) prediction plays a central role in modern computer-aided drug discovery by enabling early evaluation of pharmacokinetic behaviour and safety liabilities. This tutorial presents a reproducible computational workflow for large-scale ADMET profiling using ADMET-AI 2.0, a graph neural network-based prediction platform, applied to 200 cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2) inhibitors curated from ChEMBL release 35. Implemented within an annotated Jupyter notebook, the workflow integrates cheminformatics preprocessing, physicochemical p
papers.summary: This tutorial presents a reproducible Jupyter notebook workflow for predicting ADMET properties and toxicity of 200 CDK2 inhibitors curated from ChEMBL, using the graph neural network platform ADMET-AI 2.0 combined with RDKit for cheminformatics preprocessing. It demonstrates how to perform large-scale pharmacokinetic and safety profiling in a practical, accessible manner for computer-aided drug discovery.

papers.title: Can AI Help Repurpose Drugs to Fight Against Antibiotic Resistance?
papers.abstract: Drug repurposing and development to meet the threat of antimicrobial resistance can be costly and time-consuming, but AI models may be able to help. In this News and Perspectives article, JMIR Correspondent Sara Novak reports on recent research training models to identify candidate drugs to treat resistant infections.
papers.summary: This news and perspectives article reports on recent research that uses AI models to identify existing drugs that could be repurposed to treat antibiotic-resistant infections. It highlights how AI can accelerate and reduce the cost of drug discovery in the fight against antimicrobial resistance.

papers.title: Integrated experimental and computational study of a novel indenonaphthodiazepine[5.3.3]propellane as a potential inhibitor of Mcl-1.
papers.abstract: Myeloid cell leukemia-1 (Mcl-1) is a key anti-apoptotic protein that drives resistance to chemotherapy, making it a critical oncology target. In this study, we synthesized a new indenonaphthodiazepine[5.3.3]propellane via a one-pot multicomponent reaction and characterized its structure by FT-IR, 1H-NMR, 13C-NMR, and mass spectrometry. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations at the B3LYP/6-31G (d) level were carried out to study its electronic features and reactive centers. In molecular docking against Mcl-1, the propellane derivative showed a binding score of -5.678 kcal mol-1, outperfor
papers.summary: The authors synthesized a novel indenonaphthodiazepine[5.3.3]propellane compound via a one-pot multicomponent reaction and characterized it spectroscopically. DFT calculations and molecular docking against the anti-apoptotic protein Mcl-1 suggested favorable binding (-5.678 kcal/mol), positioning the compound as a potential oncology drug candidate. The work is preliminary, relying on computational docking without experimental validation of biological activity.

papers.title: A multimodal digital NeuroMarker platform with composite and domain-level validity for identification of mild cognitive impairment: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is a clinically heterogeneous syndrome that can represent an early manifestation of neurodegenerative disease. Diagnosis relies on assessments that are difficult to scale, leaving many individuals unidentified.
papers.summary: This study presents a multimodal digital NeuroMarker platform that combines multiple digital assessments to identify mild cognitive impairment, addressing the scalability limits of traditional clinical diagnosis. The platform demonstrates both composite and domain-level validity, suggesting it can detect MCI across its heterogeneous presentations. This cross-sectional work offers a potentially scalable screening approach for early cognitive decline.

papers.title: Biosynthetic Pathways and Regulation of Antibacterial Compounds From Endophytic Fungi: From Chemistry to Genomics and Biotechnology.
papers.abstract: Endophytic fungi are non-pathogenic symbionts that represent a rich source of structurally diverse bioactive secondary metabolites. However, genome-mining studies reveal that most of their biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) remain transcriptionally silent under standard laboratory conditions, leaving much of their chemical diversity unexplored. This review examines antibacterial natural products from endophytic fungi by integrating three complementary aspects: metabolite chemistry, biosynthetic pathways, and strategies for activating cryptic BGCs. Endophytic fungi produce polyketides, non-ribos
papers.summary: This review integrates the chemistry, biosynthetic pathways, and genomic regulation of antibacterial natural products from endophytic fungi. It highlights that most biosynthetic gene clusters in these fungi remain silent under standard laboratory conditions, and surveys strategies for activating cryptic BGCs to unlock unexplored chemical diversity.

papers.title: Interpretable Drug-Target Prediction via Geometric Alignment: A Linear Alternative to Deep Architectural Complexity.
papers.abstract: Designing selective kinase inhibitors is a multiobjective optimization problem constrained by the structural conservation of the human kinome, along with the lack of high-quality interaction data. Traditional deep learning methods often train complex neural networks directly on small datasets and fail to generalize to new chemical scaffolds. To this end, we present Geometric Manifold Alignment, a novel linear approach that shifts away from architectural complexity. We introduce Multi-View Linear Manifold (MVLM), which aligns the latent spaces of ChemBERTa (small molecules) and ESM-2 (protein s
papers.summary: The authors propose Multi-View Linear Manifold (MVLM), a linear method that aligns latent embeddings from ChemBERTa (for small molecules) and ESM-2 (for proteins) to predict kinase inhibitor–target interactions. By replacing complex deep architectures with geometric manifold alignment, the approach aims to improve generalization to new chemical scaffolds while remaining interpretable, addressing data scarcity in kinase drug discovery.

papers.title: AI-Enabled Animal Behavior Analysis for Translational Pharmacology and Therapeutic Discovery.
papers.abstract: Animal behavior is a critical endpoint in preclinical pharmacology, toxicology, and therapeutic discovery, yet conventional behavioral scoring remains labor-intensive, low-dimensional, and difficult to reproduce across laboratories. Artificial intelligence (AI) can now quantify behavior from video with greater spatial, temporal, and phenotypic resolution. This review summarizes how object detection, markerless pose estimation, unsupervised behavioral segmentation, foundation models, and autonomous analysis agents are reshaping behavioral phenotyping. General-purpose object detectors rapidly lo
papers.summary: This review discusses how AI methods—including object detection, markerless pose estimation, unsupervised behavioral segmentation, foundation models, and autonomous analysis agents—are transforming animal behavior quantification for preclinical pharmacology and therapeutic discovery. These approaches offer higher spatial, temporal, and phenotypic resolution than conventional manual scoring, which is labor-intensive, low-dimensional, and poorly reproducible across labs.

papers.title: UPLC-MS/MS-GNPS based metabolite profiling and inhibitory potential of Vitex negundo L. leaves against Shiga toxins: Applications for biodegradable films with antibacterial properties.
papers.abstract: Antibiotic therapy for STEC O157:H7 infections induces Shiga toxin release, highlighting the need for alternative, food-compatible antimicrobial strategies. The ethanolic leaf extract of Vitex negundo L. was characterized by UPLC-qTOF-MS/MS, integrated with Feature-Based Molecular Networking (GNPS), which putatively annotated 56 metabolites. Computational screening of all annotated compounds against the Stx1 and Stx2 B-subunits identified compound 8, an iridoid glycoside, as the top-ranked candidate with predicted Stx1-binding potential (ΔG = -6.9 kcal/mol; Ki = 8.7 µM). Over 100 ns of molecul
papers.summary: The authors profiled the ethanolic leaf extract of Vitex negundo using UPLC-qTOF-MS/MS combined with GNPS molecular networking, putatively annotating 56 metabolites. Computational docking and molecular dynamics identified an iridoid glycoside as a top candidate binder of the Shiga toxin B-subunits, and the extract was incorporated into biodegradable films with antibacterial properties. The work is exploratory and in silico, with no direct experimental validation of toxin neutralization reported in the abstract.

papers.title: Integrative network pharmacology and experimental evaluation reveal TNBC-related biological activity and toxicity of Euphorbia umbellata crude latex.
papers.abstract: Euphorbia umbellata latex is used in Brazilian traditional medicine, including empirically for cancer treatment. However, its chemical composition, molecular targets, pharmacological properties, and biological effects in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remain insufficiently characterized. This study investigated the TNBC-related biological activity and toxicity of E. umbellata crude latex by integrating computational analyses with experimental evaluation in a 4T1 cell model. Eighteen compounds previously identified in E. umbellata crude latex were curated from phytochemical studies and ev
papers.summary: This study combined computational network pharmacology with experimental testing in 4T1 triple-negative breast cancer cells to characterize the anti-cancer activity and toxicity of Euphorbia umbellata crude latex, a Brazilian traditional medicine. The authors curated 18 known latex compounds and mapped their predicted molecular targets to TNBC-related pathways, then validated key findings experimentally. The work provides an initial integrative assessment of the latex's pharmacological potential and safety profile for TNBC.

papers.title: Integrative Single-Cell and Bulk RNA Sequencing Analysis Identifies Ion Channel-Related Biomarkers in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
papers.abstract: Human ion channel genes (HICGs), as core effectors of transmembrane signal transduction, play a critical role in the initiation and progression of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD); however, the underlying mechanisms remain largely unclear. This study aimed to investigate the potential value of ion channel genes in COPD.
papers.journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing data to identify ion channel-related genes as potential biomarkers in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). The authors highlight that human ion channel genes are core effectors of transmembrane signaling and may contribute to COPD onset and progression, but their specific roles remain poorly understood. The work aims to establish the potential diagnostic or mechanistic value of these genes in COPD.

papers.title: Bone morphogenetic protein 4 meets artificial intelligence: a comprehensive review of AI-driven advances in drug discovery, structural modeling, and clinical translation.
papers.abstract: Bone Morphogenetic Protein 4 (BMP4), a member of the transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) superfamily, plays pivotal roles in embryonic development, tissue homeostasis, and disease pathogenesis-including cancer, fibrosis, and fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP). The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methodologies over the past 5 years has created unprecedented opportunities for understanding and therapeutically targeting BMP4 biology at multiple scales, from atomic-resolution structure prediction to population-level clinical prognostication.
papers.summary: This review surveys how AI and machine learning have been applied to BMP4 research over the past five years, spanning structure prediction, drug discovery, and clinical prognostication. It frames BMP4's roles in development, cancer, fibrosis, and FOP, and catalogs AI-driven approaches for understanding and therapeutically targeting this TGF-β family ligand. The paper is a synthesis of existing work rather than a new empirical study.

papers.title: Hupehenine suppresses tumor cell phenotypes and modulates macrophage marker profiles in a diabeticmimetic colorectal cancer model.
papers.abstract: Diabetes is associated with increased colorectal cancer (CRC) risk and mortality, but the molecular links remain incompletely understood. We aimed to characterize shared molecular features of diabetes and CRC, and identify compounds capable of modulating the candidate axis at this interface.
papers.summary: This study identifies shared molecular features between diabetes and colorectal cancer and tests whether the natural compound hupehenine can modulate these pathways. Using a diabetic-mimetic CRC model, the authors show that hupehenine suppresses tumor cell phenotypes and alters macrophage marker profiles, suggesting a potential therapeutic axis at the diabetes–cancer interface.

papers.title: Virology-aware artificial intelligence for respiratory antiviral discovery: from molecular docking biases to RdRp-centered benchmarking.
papers.abstract: Respiratory RNA viruses remain a persistent threat because they combine high transmissibility, rapid evolution, immune escape, zoonotic spillover, and incomplete therapeutic coverage. RNA-dependent RNA polymerases (RdRps) and polymerase complexes are among the most conserved and pharmacologically actionable viral targets, yet they are also challenging computational targets because their ligandable states depend on RNA templates, cofactors, divalent metals, multidomain architecture, and conformational transitions. Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), geometri
papers.summary: This perspective argues that AI-driven discovery of respiratory antivirals must account for virology-specific features of RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) targets, such as RNA templates, metal cofactors, and conformational states, rather than relying on generic docking pipelines. It highlights biases in conventional molecular docking and proposes RdRp-centered benchmarking to make AI models more biologically realistic and useful for antiviral development.

papers.title: Research progress on the application of multi-scale computational methods in the research and development of anti-tuberculosis infection drugs.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), driven by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), remains a leading cause of mortality from infectious disease worldwide.​ The global dissemination of multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) strains-coupled with protracted treatment regimens and the persistence of latent infection-has not only compromised first-line chemotherapies but also underscored the stagnation of conventional drug development pipelines. In this review, we systematically synthesize how multi-scale computational strategies are reshaping anti-TB drug discovery and explicitly delineate the
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how multi-scale computational approaches—spanning molecular docking, molecular dynamics, network analysis, and machine learning—are being applied to anti-tuberculosis drug discovery. It highlights how these methods can accelerate target identification and compound screening against drug-resistant Mtb strains, addressing the stagnation of conventional development pipelines.

papers.title: Integrative transcriptomic and computational analysis associates Ms4a6c+ macrophages with fibrosis in radiation proctitis and computationally nominates MOTS-c as a candidate modulator.
papers.abstract: Chronic radiation proctitis (CRP) represents a significant clinical challenge characterized by irreversible fibrosis and a lack of specific pharmacological interventions. This study aimed to elucidate the cellular mechanisms underlying impaired tissue repair to identify novel therapeutic targets.
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic profiling with computational analyses to characterize the cellular landscape of chronic radiation proctitis, identifying Ms4a6c+ macrophages as associated with fibrotic progression. Through computational nomination, the mitochondrial-derived peptide MOTS-c is proposed as a candidate modulator of this fibrotic process. The work is exploratory and hypothesis-generating, with findings requiring experimental validation.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence and anti-cancer drugs: advancing discovery, personalization, and precision oncology.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing the way we discover anticancer drugs. It tackles the problems of traditional methods, such as prolonged timelines for drug development, higher costs, and substantial inter-patient heterogeneity. This review explains how AI is applied throughout the cancer drug pipeline. This includes target identification, virtual screening of compounds, molecular docking, and predicting pharmacokinetics. We explore how machine learning models speed up hit-to-lead optimization, improve clinical trial design by stratifying patients, and allow for real-time toxicity monit
papers.summary: This review surveys how artificial intelligence is being applied across the anticancer drug development pipeline, from target identification and virtual screening through molecular docking, pharmacokinetic prediction, and hit-to-lead optimization. It also discusses how machine learning can improve clinical trial design via patient stratification and enable real-time toxicity monitoring for precision oncology. The paper is an overview rather than a primary research contribution.

papers.title: Cytochrome P450 inhibitors: friends or foes?
papers.abstract: Cytochrome P450 (CYP450) enzymes play a central role in the metabolism of xenobiotics and endogenous compounds, influencing drug pharmacokinetics, efficacy, and safety. Inhibition of these enzymes has traditionally been viewed as a major liability in drug discovery due to its association with drug-drug interactions (DDIs), toxicity, and metabolic instability. However, inhibition of specific CYP450 isoforms has emerged as a powerful therapeutic strategy in multiple disease areas, including cancer and infectious diseases. This review presents a comprehensive analysis of data and regulatory guida
papers.summary: This review examines cytochrome P450 inhibitors from both angles: as a traditional liability in drug discovery due to drug-drug interactions and toxicity, and as an emerging therapeutic strategy for cancer and infectious diseases. It synthesizes data and regulatory guidance to argue that isoform-specific CYP450 inhibition can be a deliberate, beneficial design goal rather than only a risk to be avoided.

papers.title: Exploration or exploitation? The double-edged effects of AI use modes on radical creativity: evidence from AI-enabled drug discovery.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been widely adopted in corporate innovation activities, yet prior research has not reached a consensus on whether it is more conducive to incremental or radical innovation. For radical innovation, which depends on highly novel ideas, realizing the value of AI depends not only on whether AI is adopted but, more importantly, on whether employees can use it creatively to transcend established knowledge boundaries. Drawing on environmental dynamism and the exploration-exploitation perspective, this study develops a theoretical model linking leaders' perceptions of
papers.summary: This study examines how different modes of AI use (exploration vs. exploitation) affect radical creativity in AI-enabled drug discovery, drawing on the exploration-exploitation framework and environmental dynamism. It proposes a theoretical model linking leaders' perceptions to employee creative outcomes, arguing that AI's value for radical innovation depends on how creatively employees use it to transcend established knowledge boundaries. The work is a conceptual/psychological model rather than an empirical bioinformatics study.

papers.title: SCOPE-based target and pathway enrichment identifies the histamine H1 receptor as a regulator of exodosis.
papers.abstract: Phenotypic screening enables discovery of small molecules without requiring predefined targets, but mechanistic interpretation remains challenging due to polypharmacology and pathway complexity.
papers.summary: The authors apply SCOPE, a target and pathway enrichment method, to phenotypic screening data to identify mechanisms of action. They identify the histamine H1 receptor as a regulator of exodosis, demonstrating how enrichment analysis can deconvolute polypharmacology and reveal pathway-level regulators from phenotypic screens.

papers.title: Integrated in vitro and in silico assessment of antimicrobial, chemical antioxidant, and cytotoxic activities of endophytic Aspergillus sp. GK1 isolated from Mentha spicata roots.
papers.abstract: Medicinal plants are a source of structurally diverse endophytic fungi which harbor significant pharmaceutical potential.
papers.summary: This study isolated the endophytic fungus Aspergillus sp. GK1 from Mentha spicata roots and characterized its secondary metabolites. Extracts showed antimicrobial and antioxidant activity in vitro, with cytotoxicity against cell lines, and computational (in silico) docking analyses were used to predict which compounds might be responsible. The work supports endophytic fungi from medicinal plants as a source of bioactive natural products, though the findings are preliminary and based on crude extracts.

papers.title: An m5C-associated NSUN5-YBX1-CENPF programme marks melanoma cell states and immune features.
papers.abstract: RNA 5-methylcytosine (m5C)-associated programmes may help characterise melanoma cell states and their immune context. We investigated an NSUN5-YBX1-CENPF (NYC) programme using patient-matched sequencing, experimental perturbation and multiscale transcriptomic analyses.
papers.summary: This study identifies an RNA m5C-associated regulatory programme (NSUN5-YBX1-CENPF, or NYC) that characterises distinct melanoma cell states and correlates with immune features in patient tumours. Using matched patient sequencing, experimental perturbation, and multiscale transcriptomic analyses, the authors link this epitranscriptomic axis to melanoma heterogeneity and immune context.

papers.title: Plasmid-Mediated AmpC Detection in Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae: In Vitro Prevalence and In Silico Inhibitor Design.
papers.abstract: This study investigated the prevalence of AmpC beta-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae in clinical specimens collected in Lahore, Pakistan, and aimed to identify potential inhibitors targeting AmpC beta-lactamases.
papers.journal: The Canadian journal of infectious diseases & medical microbiology = Journal canadien des maladies infectieuses et de la microbiologie medicale
papers.summary: This study screened clinical E. coli and K. pneumoniae isolates from Lahore, Pakistan for plasmid-mediated AmpC beta-lactamase production, establishing local prevalence of these antibiotic-resistance enzymes. The authors then used computational (in silico) docking approaches to identify candidate small-molecule inhibitors targeting AmpC beta-lactamases. The work combines regional surveillance with early-stage structure-based drug design against a clinically important resistance mechanism.

papers.title: Investigating potential molecular mechanisms linking 6PPD-quinone exposure to Intervertebral Disc Degeneration: A network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulation study.
papers.abstract: As an emerging pollutant derived from tire rubber, 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q) has raised public health concerns due to widespread environmental exposure; however, its potential toxicological effects on avascular tissues such as intervertebral discs remain unclear. This study integrated network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation to investigate the potential mechanisms linking 6PPD-Q exposure to intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD). ADMET toxicological predictions indicated high model-predicted probabilities for SR-MMP and SR-ARE activation. Through multidimensio
papers.summary: This study uses network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to predict how the environmental pollutant 6PPD-quinone might contribute to intervertebral disc degeneration. The authors identify potential molecular targets and pathways, suggesting mechanistic hypotheses for pollutant-driven disc degeneration. The work is entirely computational and provides predictions that require experimental validation.
